title: Briefings mark lessons whose code changed after their last check (#93)

issues.title: Flag stale lessons in the briefing itself
issues.body:
A lesson whose governed files changed after its last `okl verify` is only reported by `okl drift` and the CI gate. The briefing that puts it in front of the agent says nothing, so the agent trusts a lesson that may no longer hold.

**Proposal:** when `okl check` briefs a lesson that has drifted (or that governs files and was never verified), mark it in the briefing, e.g. `⚠ stale: app/orders.py changed since this was last verified`, so the agent treats it as a lead to confirm rather than a rule. Reuse the drift logic; only the briefed lessons are checked, so it stays cheap.

**Why:** GitHub Copilot Memory re-checks a memory's citations against the current branch before using it; Codified Context warns at session start when code changed without its spec. Evidence: [What keeps an agent setup true](https://emeraldleaf.dev/writing/what-keeps-an-agent-setup-true/) (2026-10-01).

title: check: a relevance floor before the top-12 cutoff

issues.title: Briefing precision: a relevance floor before the top-12 cutoff, measured
issues.body:
## Why

The briefing always fills its twelve slots. The search is an OR of the task's subject words, ranked by BM25, cut at the limit, with no floor on how well a record matched. On a short or generic prompt that means twelve records chosen by one shared word. From the probe in PR #256 (`evals/results/probe-rephrase-20261021.txt`, six prompts taken verbatim from one session, this repo's interests):

| prompt | records returned | matched one word only | the word |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| "this seems like a major point to scrutinize" | 12 | 12 | point, major |
| "what about the org knowledge idea, is that a niche?" | 10 | 10 | org |
| "give me a doc for that too" | 12 | 12 | give, doc |
| "how do we come up with a good plan for governing github copilot and mcp" | 12 | 10 | plan, governing, come |

Those twelve arrive in the agent's context as imperatives under "Do this", including a remote-sensing compositing rule for the word "point". The hook output for the first prompt is about 8,800 characters, roughly 2,200 tokens, on every such prompt. This is the recorded defect "ranking works, filtering doesn't" in its remaining form: the cutoff bounded the count, not the relevance.

## What to do

Add a relevance floor before the cutoff, and report what it removed:

- A record is briefed only if it matches **two or more** of the task's subject words, or one word when the task has only one. On the probe this keeps 0, 4, 0, 0, 2 and 3 of the twelve for the six prompts above, and keeps **all eight** authored eval tasks' governing records (each matches 2 to 10 words). A rarity-based floor (a word in at most 3% of the store) was also tried and loses two of the eight, so it is the wrong shape.
- When the floor empties the briefing, say so in the hook line: "0 relevant lessons; 12 weak matches trimmed" is a different fact from "0 lessons in the store", and both differ from silence.
- `okl check --format json` gains the matched-word count per record and the number trimmed by the floor, so the exposure log can keep it.

## Measure before merging

`evals/preflight.py` must stay green (it already asserts each task's record is present). Re-run `evals/probe_rephrase.py` and commit the receipt beside the one in PR #256; the floor must not change any "yes" in its recall table. Then one A/B on the §4m instrument, since a shorter briefing is also a cheaper one and #234 is already measuring briefing size.

issues.title: Docs that say 'not yet measured' should fail once the measurement lands
issues.body:
**Problem.** Docs keep saying something is "not yet measured" after the measurement has landed. A review has caught this three times. Most recently, the anatomy sheet (#333) said all three of these were unmeasured, though each had a result:
- the gate's drift (§4ae, §4af, §4ah);
- whether an agent opens a one-line lesson (§4ab);
- the shared-word miss, which no longer holds with the warm model on.

Nothing ties an open-question sentence to the question it is waiting on, so nothing notices when that question is answered.

**Proposal.** `tests/test_docs.py` keeps a list of every "not (yet) measured", "unmeasured" or "still open" sentence in the README, `docs/` and the overview sheets. Each entry names the open question it stands for. When a REPORT result settles one, its "What follows" names the entry, and the test fails while the settled sentence is still in the docs. The test also fails on an unlisted sentence of that kind, so a new one has to name its question.

This is the same shape as `DOC_FIGURES`, which holds each published size to its receipt line.

**Done when:** the test exists, lists the current sentences with their questions, and was proven red on a sentence whose question is settled.

issues.title: Stack detection reads only the repo root's package.json and Python manifests
issues.body:
## Where it stands (main, 24784b4)
`_detect_stacks` (`src/okl/cli/install.py:354`) reads `package.json` and the Python manifests (`pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt`, `setup.py`) at the repo root only. .NET is the exception: it already globs `*/*.csproj` and `*/*/*.csproj`. A monorepo that keeps its UI in `app/frontend-react/package.json` is never detected as `react`, so the frontend pack is never offered and its subjects never reach the interests.

## Proposal
Look one or two directory levels down for these manifests too, with the excludes `first()` already applies (`.git`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv`, `bin`, `obj`). Name the file that showed each stack, as now.

## Tests
- A fixture with `app/web/package.json` that depends on `react` is detected as `react (app/web/package.json)`.
- One under `node_modules/` is not detected.
- A root manifest still wins over a nested one.

title: The relevance floor weighs a one-word match by how common the word is (REPORT §4v)

issues.title: Experiment: the floor's one-word rule weighted by how common the word is in the store
issues.body:
Part of #258; beside #263 (which asks the opposite question for rare identifier-like words) and after REPORT §4u.

## Why

The relevance floor admits a lesson that shares two subject words with the prompt, or one word that sits in the lesson's title or symptom. Written for words like "price" or "endpoint", the one-word rule also admits every lesson whose title holds "doc", "update" or "search", because a word's weight does not depend on how many lessons carry it. On the six precision prompts three still return 9 to 12 lessons (receipt `probe-rephrase-20261024-semwords-off-fulltext.txt`: 4, 11, 0, 11, 9, 12), all through one common title word. §4u traced the paraphrase misses to the same place: generic shared words keep fifteen lessons above the right one.

The probe already measures the ingredient: section B prints, for every returned lesson, the document frequency of its rarest matched word, and section C shows what a flat line would cost. At "one word admits only when it is in 3% of lessons or fewer", one authored task is lost (`idor_endpoint`, whose lesson matches only common words), so the line is not a constant to pick by hand.

## Proposal

A module constant in `core`, `COMMON_WORD_SHARE` (None today): when a lesson's only shared word is in more than that share of the store's lessons, the one-word rule does not apply and the lesson needs a second shared word. Two shared words always suffice; a one-word alias matched whole and the identifier-like words #263 proposes stay strong regardless. The document-frequency table is one query per check (or a cached count per word) and costs nothing at this scale.

## Pre-registration (REPORT §4v, written before the run)

- **Selection:** a grid over shares (3%, 5%, 10%, 15%, 25%) on the selection set (the probe's own rephrasings and the authored tasks) and the six prompts, with the authored row held at 8 of 8 as a hard constraint; the line is the largest share that keeps the authored row and reduces the three heavy prompts.
- **Measure:** `evals/probe_rephrase.py` at one commit, the knob off (control) and at the chosen line, full-text and linear.
- **Predictions:** at least two of the three heavy prompts drop below 6 lessons; held-out recall by variant does not fall; the authored row stays 8.
- **Falsifiers:** any held-out row falls; or the authored row falls; or no prompt drops. Then the knob stays at None with the receipt kept.
- **Cost:** none at runtime beyond one count query; the probe runs in a minute.

## Acceptance

The grid receipt, the probe receipts, §4v with the result, the knob at its measured value or at None, and the rejection summary line in the probe (see #179) showing the before and after.

title: A renamed seed pack takes the records a store holds under its old name with it (#379)

issues.title: Renamed seed packs orphan the records of stores seeded before the rename
issues.body:
## Where it stands (main, 24784b4)
A seed record's id is `seed:<pack>:<key>` (`src/okl/seed.py`), and `okl seed --refresh` finds the packs to refresh from the ids already in the store. b28bf64 renamed ten packs when it made project identities generic, keeping their keys: `novacraft-*` became `dotnet-*` and `frontend-canon`, `san-juan-*` became `geospatial-*`, and one RAG defects pack became `rag-defects`. A store seeded before the rename holds the old ids. Refresh cannot update them (one consumer repo has 9 such records from one pack), and seeding a renamed pack stores them a second time under new ids.

## Proposal
Give `seed/` a rename map (old pack name → new), with the ten renames above. Refresh and import then resolve an old id to the new pack and move the record to the new id, keeping its verification. A deduplication pass by pack key on import is the alternative.

## Tests
- A store seeded under the old pack name refreshes from the renamed pack, leaving no duplicate. The record's verification and id history survive.
- Seeding the renamed pack into that store adds nothing.

issues.title: Hooks: fall through when a pinned okl's interpreter is gone (exit 126/127) instead of blocking
issues.body:
Split out of #140. That issue's fix section asked to "accept a candidate only if it can run". #151 does this for the `<python> -m okl` form (the python must `import okl`), but a pinned **path** is still accepted on `command -v` alone. Main behaves the same way, so this is not a regression.

## What happens

A pipx or venv `okl` script whose shebang interpreter is gone, for example after a Homebrew python upgrade removed the version the venv was built on. The file still exists and is executable, so `command -v` accepts the pin. The prompt hook then runs it, gets exit 126 (`bad interpreter`), and blocks the prompt, **even when a working okl is on `PATH`**. The Stop hook asks its question in a repo where `okl record` cannot run.

The deep review of #151 reproduced this on the branch and on main.

## Options

- **Fall through on 126/127, with no added cost per prompt** (preferred). When the check run exits 126 or 127 and okl came from a pinned layer, resume resolution at the next layer and run once more. Today the retry loop already treats 126/127 as "will not heal", so it is the natural place for this.
- Probe each path pin before using it, as the pre-push hook does (`<candidate> drift --help`). That costs about 50 ms on every prompt for every user, not only those with a broken pin, so it is the worse trade.

## Acceptance

- [ ] With a pinned okl whose shebang interpreter is missing and a working okl on `PATH`, the prompt hook delivers the briefing and the Stop hook asks its question
- [ ] With nothing else to fall back on, the block names the pin and says to re-run `okl init`, and no ENOENT phrasing reaches stderr
- [ ] No extra process runs on the path where the pin works

issues.title: A/B harness scores a plan with no code as a clean run
issues.body:
In `ab-20261010-2314.json` (REPORT §4j), the briefed `idor_endpoint` sample 1 returned a plan, not code. The judge's own reason says so:

> No actual code was submitted—only a plan describing intended implementation; the developer claims IDOR-safe scoping by buyer_id with 404 on non-match, but code must be audited to verify.

The harness still scored it `reproduced: false`, so it counted as a clean briefed run. A sample with no implementation shows nothing either way. Counted as clean, it flatters whichever arm it lands in. (Found by CodeRabbit on #162.)

**Scope checked:** a text scan of every committed receipt's judge reasons found only this one plan-only sample. The other two matches were real implementations that reproduced the defect.

**Proposed fix:**
- The judge returns `implemented: bool` alongside `defect_reproduced`.
- The harness counts `implemented: false` as a failure (unevaluable): kept in `failures`, out of the denominators, and counted toward the 20% usability bar.
- The judge prompt is part of the instrument, so this should land with a REPORT pre-registration, like §4i's and §4j's.

**Also worth adding while there:** record the resolved model id per run, not only the alias (review item R12). §4j's baseline fell 26 points, and the receipt can't say whether the model changed.

title: okl warm stop: answered when it stops a server, and a stop stays (#320)

issues.title: okl warm stop reports no server when one answered slower than the prompt's 0.5 s budget
issues.body:
**The defect.** `warm.stop()` sends the stop request with `TIMEOUT_S` (0.5 s), the budget a prompt allows for its vector. A server that takes longer than that to answer still receives the request and exits, but the client times out first, so `stop()` returns False. `okl warm stop` then reports that no server answered, even though it stopped one. `src/okl/warm.py:464-473`.

**Seen.** On #312's CI, 2026-10-31, `tests/test_warm.py::test_the_server_answers_ping_embed_and_stop` failed on Python 3.11 only, at `assert warm.stop() is True`, with the other Pythons green on the same commit. #312 does not touch `warm.py`. A busy runner is enough to push the server's answer past 0.5 s.

**Fix.** Give `stop` (and `ping` when a person runs `okl warm status`) a timeout of its own, a few seconds, since nothing waits on it the way a prompt does. Keep `TIMEOUT_S` for the prompt's embed. Add a test that slows the server's answer past `TIMEOUT_S` and still expects `stop()` to be True, and check that it fails before the fix.

title: doctor, init and metric say what the interests hide (#374)

issues.title: A repo set up before a default interest never gets it, and nothing says how many lessons its interests hide
issues.body:
## Where it stands (main, 24784b4, 2026-11-06)
- `_init_interests` (`src/okl/cli/install.py:613`) only fills an empty interest list. That is deliberate since #340: a re-run never overrides a list someone chose. Detection has since added `security` and `method`, because the portable lessons are filed under them. A repo configured before that change keeps its narrower list through every upgrade.
- `core._in_scope` (`src/okl/core.py:49`) hides every org lesson whose subjects are outside the list. One consumer repo was configured in July with five interests and neither of those two. In it, 26 of 70 org lessons never reached a briefing, among them the authorization-test and IDOR lessons.
- `okl metric` reported "42 of 45 never shown". Its denominator, "lessons this repo can be briefed", already leaves the hidden ones out (`core.exposure_report` counts only what `_in_scope` passes). So the report never mentioned the other 26, and nobody looked.

## Proposal
1. `okl doctor` and a re-run of `okl init` report how many org lessons the interests hide. They name the default subjects the config lacks, with the command that adds them. Neither changes the list, so #340's rule stands.
2. `okl metric` reports the count the interests hide, beside the lessons this repo can be briefed.

## Tests
- A store holds an org lesson tagged only `security`, and the config lacks `security`. `okl doctor` names the lesson and the missing subject.
- A re-run of `okl init` prints the offer and leaves `interests` unchanged.
- `okl metric` counts that lesson as hidden by interests.

Related: #340, #91.

issues.title: A prompt with no text is briefed on the last commit's subject
issues.body:
Sending an image (or a file) with no text reaches the UserPromptSubmit hook as an empty prompt. The hook then falls back to `git log -1`'s subject as the task, so the agent is briefed twelve lessons about unrelated work. Seen 2026-10-11: an image-only prompt was briefed on "Re-verify after merging the judge fix".

R7 (#178) made a prompt with no subject brief nothing; this path skips it, because the hook substitutes a task before okl sees the prompt.

Expected: a prompt event with no text briefs nothing and says so. The last-resort task stays for a run with no prompt event at all. It must not send an empty task to okl, since okl before R7 answers one with every lesson.
